name: Permito
tagline: Self-hosted cookie banner, preference center and consent gates for React, Next.js and any site via a script tag. No network calls, no tracking, no dark patterns.
seoTitle: Permito – self-hosted cookie consent for React & Next.js
description:
Permito is a consent toolkit you ship inside your own app instead of loading from a third-party server. Optional categories are opt-in, "Reject all" carries the same weight as "Accept all", and nothing that needs consent loads before it is given.

It is built for agencies in Switzerland, Germany and Austria: German, Swiss German, English, French and Italian are included, Google Consent Mode v2 is wired in, and the Next.js helpers read consent on the server so gated content never flashes.

code.title: app/providers.tsx

free: Opt-in by default, with "Reject all" exactly as prominent as "Accept all"
No network calls and no tracking: consent is stored in your own cookie
Gate scripts, iframes and components with ConsentScript, ConsentIframe and ConsentGate
Server-safe Next.js helpers, so gated content never flashes on load
Google Consent Mode v2 with a configurable category mapping, plus consent bridges for Microsoft UET, Microsoft Clarity and Matomo
German, Swiss German, English, French, Italian, Spanish, Dutch, Polish and Portuguese built in (the last four not yet reviewed by native speakers); keyboard and screen-reader accessible
Decisions expire after a number of days you choose, Global Privacy Control is honoured on request, and a choice applies in every open tab at once
Drop-in script tag for WordPress, static sites and CMS templates, with the same banner and preference dialog, no React needed

Starting points for 15 common services (YouTube, Google Analytics 4, Meta Pixel, HubSpot and more) with provider and privacy policy URL, without cookie claims, and a size check that keeps the bundle in bounds
Vue 3 composables and plugin and Svelte stores on top of the same core engine, plus guides for Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix and Astro that read the stored decision on the server

Checked accessibility: automated WCAG 2.2 AA scans of banner, preference center and embed placeholder plus keyboard tests in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit on every change, and guides for strict Content Security Policy and Subresource Integrity
pro: Service catalog with 71 providers, each entry sourced from the provider's own documentation with a retrieval date
Cookie table for your privacy policy, generated from the same config as the banner, with a CI check that fails when it drifts
Self-hosted consent log for Next.js, Express and Fastify: hashed visitor ID, no IP address, no user agent
Scanner that reports cookies, storage and third-party requests that appear before consent
Six theme templates with checked contrast, plus a two-step banner and a modal layout
GTM container check: matches the tags of a Google Tag Manager export to catalog services before go-live and exits with 1 on findings, reading the file only
Monitoring many client sites: one scan run over a sites file, with a weekly GitHub Action template that opens one issue per site and comments only on new differences
Catalog changes per project: after an update, lists what changed for your own services and exits with 1 when the cookie table needs to be regenerated
Consent statistics from the log: acceptance rates per category and service for a period, as a German or English report for clients, without personal data
Evidence export of the consent log as NDJSON or CSV for a period, with a manifest, SHA-256 and an optional HMAC signature, plus a check that shows whether file or manifest were changed afterwards
Audit report in German or English as Markdown and HTML: configuration, site scan, catalog freshness and the evidence manifest in one document, with missing parts marked as not checked
Seals for the consent log: a keyed hash chain over the entries of a period, linked from period to period, so later changes, removals and additions are detectable; seals hold only entry IDs and hashes
Catalog texts and cookie table headings in German, English, French, Italian and Spanish, and a freshness check for CI that lists catalog entries older than a limit

WordPress plugin generator: one JSON file becomes a plugin that loads the banner, blocks scripts that other plugins enqueue by handle (also WooCommerce) and adds shortcodes for the settings link and the cookie table

notes: After cancelling, every version you already received keeps working. Only updates and repository access end.
No licence key, no phone-home. The packages never contact a server to check your licence.
Agency and Lifetime cover up to ten named people for one price: you choose the number of seats at checkout and assign them in Polar. Your clients and their websites need no licence of their own.
Checkout, invoices and VAT are handled by Polar as merchant of record.

faq.a: Every person on your team who works with the Pro packages. Freelancer covers one person. Agency and Lifetime cover up to ten named people for the same price: you pick the number of seats at checkout, assign them in Polar, and each person connects their own GitHub account. For eleven or more, get in touch.
Every version you already received keeps working, in every project you used it in. Only new updates and access to the private repository end.

faq.q: Do my clients need their own licence?
faq.a: No. The licence covers the people building the sites. The websites you deliver and the clients who own them need nothing.

faq.q: Is there a licence key or usage tracking?
faq.a: No. The packages are installed from a private GitHub Packages registry and never contact a licence server.

faq.q: Who issues the invoice, and is VAT included?
faq.a: Polar sells Permito Pro as merchant of record. It handles checkout, invoices and VAT for your country.

faq.q: Can I use the open-source part on its own?
faq.a: Yes. @permitojs/core and @permitojs/react are MIT-licensed and complete without Pro.
